This paper studies the generalization of preference optimization under noisy feedback. It focuses on a broad family of preference optimization losses and establishes generalization guarantees under this setting. Theoretical analysis shows that the generalization bound increases as the noise rate grows. Empirical results are provided to support the theoretical findings.
